processed_hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ ، أَنّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ : " مَنْ غَيَّرَ دِينَهُ فَاضْرِبُوا عُنُقَهُ "
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Yahya narrated to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever changes his religion, then strike his neck (i.e., execute him).'

processed_hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبْدٍ الْقَارِيِّ ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : قَدِمَ عَلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَجُلٌ مِنْ قِبَلِ أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ ، فَسَأَلَهُ عَنِ النَّاسِ ، فَأَخْبَرَهُ ، ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ عُمَرُ : " هَلْ كَانَ فِيكُمْ مِنْ مُغَرِّبَةِ خَبَرٍ ؟ " فَقَالَ : نَعَمْ ، رَجُلٌ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ إِسْلَامِهِ " . قَالَ : فَمَا فَعَلْتُمْ بِهِ ؟ قَالَ : قَرَّبْنَاهُ فَضَرَبْنَا عُنُقَهُ . فَقَالَ عُمَرُ : " أَفَلَا حَبَسْتُمُوهُ ثَلَاثًا وَأَطْعَمْتُمُوهُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ رَغِيفًا وَاسْتَتَبْتُمُوهُ لَعَلَّهُ يَتُوبُ وَيُرَاجِعُ أَمْرَ اللَّهِ " . ثُمَّ قَالَ عُمَرُ : " اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي لَمْ أَحْضُرْ ، وَلَمْ آمُرْ ، وَلَمْ أَرْضَ إِذْ بَلَغَنِي "
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Qari, from his father, who said: A man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, so he asked him about the people, and he informed him. Then Umar said to him: 'Has there been any strange news among you?' He said: 'Yes, a man who disbelieved after his Islam.' He said: 'So what did you do with him?' He said: 'We brought him forward and struck his neck.' So Umar said: 'Why did you not imprison him for three days and feed him a loaf of bread each day and ask him to repent, perhaps he would repent and return to the command of Allah?' Then Umar said: 'O Allah, I was not present, nor did I command it, nor was I pleased when it reached me.'

processed_hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى ، عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ سُهَيْلِ بْنِ أَبِي صَالِحٍ السَّمَّانِ ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ، أَنَّ سَعْدَ بْنَ عُبَادَةَ ، قَالَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : أَرَأَيْتَ " إِنْ وَجَدْتُ مَعَ امْرَأَتِي رَجُلًا ، أَأُمْهِلُهُ حَتَّى آتِيَ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَاءَ ؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : نَعَمْ "
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah: Sa'd ibn Ubadah said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'What do you think - if I find a man with my wife, should I give him respite until I bring four witnesses?' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Yes.'

processed_hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ الْمُسَيَّبِ ، أَنَّ رَجُلًا مِنْ أَهْلِ الشَّامِ ، يُقَالُ لَهُ : ابْنُ خَيْبَرِيٍّ وَجَدَ مَعَ امْرَأَتِهِ رَجُلًا ، فَقَتَلَهُ أَوْ قَتَلَهُمَا مَعًا ، فَأَشْكَلَ عَلَى مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ الْقَضَاءُ فِيهِ ، فَكَتَبَ إِلَى أَبِي مُوسَى الْأَشْعَرِيِّ يَسْأَلُ لَهُ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَنْ ذَلِكَ ، فَسَأَلَ أَبُو مُوسَى عَنْ ذَلِكَ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ ، فَقَالَ لَهُ عَلِيٌّ : " إِنَّ هَذَا الشَّيْءَ مَا هُوَ بِأَرْضِي عَزَمْتُ عَلَيْكَ لَتُخْبِرَنِّي " . فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو مُوسَى : كَتَبَ إِلَيَّ مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ أَنْ أَسْأَلَكَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ . فَقَالَ عَلِيٌّ : " أَنَا أَبُو حَسَنٍ إِنْ لَمْ يَأْتِ بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَاءَ ، فَلْيُعْطَ بِرُمَّتِهِ "
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: A man from the people of Syria, called Ibn Khaybariy, found a man with his wife, so he killed him or killed them both together. The judgment became difficult for Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, so he wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari asking him to inquire from Ali ibn Abi Talib about that. So Abu Musa asked Ali ibn Abi Talib about that, and Ali said to him: 'This matter is not from my land. I adjure you to inform me.' So Abu Musa said to him: 'Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan wrote to me to ask you about that.' So Ali said: 'I am Abu al-Hasan - if he does not bring four witnesses, then let him be handed over entirely (for punishment).'

processed_hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ يَحْيَى : قَالَ مَالِك : عَنْ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ ، عَنْ سُنَيْنٍ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ رَجُلٌ مِنْ بَنِي سُلَيْمٍ ، أَنَّهُ وَجَدَ مَنْبُوذًا فِي زَمَانِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ ، قَالَ : فَجِئْتُ بِهِ إِلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ ، فَقَالَ : " مَا حَمَلَكَ عَلَى أَخْذِ هَذِهِ النَّسَمَةِ ؟ " فَقَالَ : وَجَدْتُهَا ضَائِعَةً فَأَخَذْتُهَا . فَقَالَ لَهُ : عَرِيفُهُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ، إِنَّهُ رَجُلٌ صَالِحٌ . فَقَالَ لَهُ عُمَرُ : " أَكَذَلِكَ ؟ " قَالَ : نَعَمْ . فَقَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ : " اذْهَبْ فَهُوَ حُرٌّ ، وَلَكَ وَلَاؤُهُ وَعَلَيْنَا نَفَقَتُهُ "
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Sunayn Abu Jamilah, a man from Banu Sulaym: He found an abandoned child during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab. He said: So I came with him to Umar ibn al-Khattab, and he said: 'What made you take this soul?' So he said: 'I found it lost, so I took it.' So his 'arif (local leader) said to him: 'O Commander of the Believers, he is a righteous man.' So Umar said to him: 'Is it so?' He said: 'Yes.' So Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'Go, for he is free, and his loyalty (wala') is to you, and his maintenance is upon us.'

processed_hadiths.arabicText: قَالَ يَحْيَى : عَنْ مَالِك ، عَنْ ابْنِ شِهَابٍ ، عَنْ عُرْوَةَ بْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ زَوْجِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ : كَانَ عُتْبَةُ بْنُ أَبِي وَقَّاصٍ عَهِدَ إِلَى أَخِيهِ سَعْدِ بْنِ أَبِي وَقَّاصٍ أَنَّ ابْنَ وَلِيدَةِ زَمْعَةَ مِنِّي فَاقْبِضْهُ إِلَيْكَ ، قَالَتْ : فَلَمَّا كَانَ عَامُ الْفَتْحِ ، أَخَذَهُ سَعْدٌ ، وَقَالَ : ابْنُ أَخِي ، قَدْ كَانَ عَهِدَ إِلَيَّ فِيهِ ، فَقَامَ إِلَيْهِ عَبْدُ بْنُ زَمْعَةَ ، فَقَالَ : أَخِي ، وَابْنُ وَلِيدَةِ أَبِي ، وُلِدَ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ . فَتَسَاوَقَا إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَقَالَ سَعْدٌ : يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ، ابْنُ أَخِي ، قَدْ كَانَ عَهِدَ إِلَيَّ فِيهِ . وَقَالَ عَبْدُ بْنُ زَمْعَةَ : أَخِي وَابْنُ وَلِيدَةِ أَبِي ، وُلِدَ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ . فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : " هُوَ لَكَ يَا عَبْدُ بْنَ زَمْعَةَ " ، ثُمَّ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : " الْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ وَلِلْعَاهِرِ الْحَجَرُ " . ثُمَّ قَالَ لِسَوْدَةَ بِنْتِ زَمْعَةَ : " احْتَجِبِي مِنْهُ " لِمَا رَأَى مِنْ شَبَهِهِ بِعُتْبَةَ بْنِ أَبِي وَقَّاصٍ ، قَالَتْ : فَمَا رَآهَا حَتَّى لَقِيَ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Aishah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, she said: Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas had made a covenant with his brother Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas that 'The son of the slave-woman of Zam'ah is from me, so take him to yourself.' She said: When the Year of the Conquest came, Sa'd took him and said: 'The son of my brother - he had made a covenant with me about him.' So Abd ibn Zam'ah stood up to him and said: 'My brother, and the son of my father's slave-woman, he was born on his bed.' So they both went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Sa'd said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the son of my brother - he had made a covenant with me about him.' And Abd ibn Zam'ah said: 'My brother and the son of my father's slave-woman, he was born on his bed.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'He is yours, O Abd ibn Zam'ah.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'The child belongs to the bed (legitimate marriage), and for the adulterer is the stone.' Then he said to Sawdah bint Zam'ah: 'Veil yourself from him' - because of what he saw of his resemblance to Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas. She said: So he never saw her until he met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

potential_issues.impact: While 'an is used multiple times, all these connections are well-established: Malik's learning from al-Zuhri's students is documented, al-Zuhri's learning from Urwah is famous, and Urwah's narrations from his aunt Aishah are extensively documented. This is considered one of the golden chains (silsilah al-dhahab) in hadith transmission.

Topics: Incident of dispute over paternity of a child during the Conquest of Makkah
Principle 'the child belongs to the bed' (al-walad lil-firash)
Prophet's ﷺ judgment in paternity dispute
Instruction to Sawdah to veil from the child due to resemblance

processed_hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْهَادِي ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ الْحَارِثِ التَّيْمِيِّ ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ يَسَارٍ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي أُمَيَّةَ ، أَنّ " امْرَأَةً هَلَكَ عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا فَاعْتَدَّتْ أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْرًا ، ثُمَّ تَزَوَّجَتْ حِينَ حَلَّتْ فَمَكَثَتْ عِنْدَ زَوْجِهَا أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَنِصْفَ شَهْرٍ ، ثُمَّ وَلَدَتْ وَلَدًا تَامًّا ، فَجَاءَ زَوْجُهَا إِلَى عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ فَذَكَرَ ذَلِكَ لَهُ ، فَدَعَا عُمَرُ نِسْوَةً مِنْ نِسَاءِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ قُدَمَاءَ ، فَسَأَلَهُنَّ عَنْ ذَلِكَ ، فَقَالَتِ امْرَأَةٌ مِنْهُنَّ : أَنَا أُخْبِرُكَ عَنْ هَذِهِ الْمَرْأَةِ ، هَلَكَ عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا حِينَ حَمَلَتْ مِنْهُ ، فَأُهْرِيقَتْ عَلَيْهِ الدِّمَاءُ ، فَحَشَّ وَلَدُهَا فِي بَطْنِهَا ، فَلَمَّا أَصَابَهَا زَوْجُهَا الَّذِي نَكَحَهَا وَأَصَابَ الْوَلَدَ الْمَاءُ تَحَرَّكَ الْوَلَدُ فِي بَطْنِهَا وَكَبِرَ . فَصَدَّقَهَا عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ وَفَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا ، وَقَالَ عُمَرُ : " أَمَا إِنَّهُ لَمْ يَبْلُغْنِي عَنْكُمَا إِلَّا خَيْرٌ " ، وَأَلْحَقَ الْوَلَدَ بِالْأَوَّلِ
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah: A woman whose husband died, so she observed the waiting period of four months and ten days, then she married when her waiting period ended. She remained with her husband for four months and half a month, then she gave birth to a fully-formed child. So her husband came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and mentioned that to him. So Umar called elderly women from among the women of the pre-Islamic era and asked them about that. So a woman among them said: 'I will inform you about this woman - her husband died when she had conceived from him, so blood was poured upon it (the fetus), and her child dried up in her belly. When her husband who married her had relations with her and the water (semen) reached the child, the child moved in her belly and grew.' So Umar ibn al-Khattab believed her and separated between them, and Umar said: 'Indeed, nothing has reached me about you two except good,' and he attributed the child to the first (husband).

processed_hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي مَالِك ، عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ يَسَارٍ ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ كَانَ يُلِيطُ أَوْلَادَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ بِمَنِ ادَّعَاهُمْ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ ، " فَأَتَى رَجُلَانِ كِلَاهُمَا يَدَّعِي وَلَدَ امْرَأَةٍ ، فَدَعَا عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ قَائِفًا ، فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِمَا ، فَقَالَ الْقَائِفُ : لَقَدِ اشْتَرَكَا فِيهِ ، فَضَرَبَهُ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ بِالدِّرَّةِ ، ثُمَّ دَعَا الْمَرْأَةَ ، فَقَالَ : " أَخْبِرِينِي خَبَرَكِ " . فَقَالَتْ : كَانَ هَذَا لِأَحَدِ الرَّجُلَيْنِ يَأْتِينِي وَهِيَ فِي إِبِلٍ لِأَهْلِهَا ، فَلَا يُفَارِقُهَا حَتَّى يَظُنَّ وَتَظُنَّ أَنَّهُ قَدِ اسْتَمَرَّ بِهَا حَبَلٌ ، ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَ عَنْهَا فَأُهْرِيقَتْ عَلَيْهِ دِمَاءٌ ، ثُمَّ خَلَفَ عَلَيْهَا هَذَا تَعْنِي الْآخَرَ ، فَلَا أَدْرِي مِنْ أَيِّهِمَا هُوَ . قَالَ : فَكَبَّرَ الْقَائِفُ ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ لِلْغُلَامِ : " وَالِ أَيَّهُمَا شِئْتَ "
processed_hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Sulayman ibn Yasar: Umar ibn al-Khattab used to attach children from the pre-Islamic era to whoever claimed them in Islam. So two men came, each of them claiming a woman's child. So Umar ibn al-Khattab called a qa'if (physiognomist skilled in determining lineage). He looked at them, and the qa'if said: 'They have both shared in him.' So Umar ibn al-Khattab struck him with the whip. Then he called the woman and said: 'Inform me of your story.' So she said: 'This one - meaning one of the two men - used to come to me when she was with her family's camels, and he would not leave her until he thought and she thought that pregnancy had been established with her. Then he left her, and blood was poured upon it (the pregnancy). Then this one - meaning the other - came after him. So I do not know which of them he is from.' He said: So the qa'if said 'Allahu Akbar.' So Umar said to the boy: 'Take as guardian whichever of them you wish.'
